[approach_variants] Snow banked against the base into early summer .

routes.name: Raven Ridge Traverse
routes.whyDry: Approach gully and ridge snow-free in season.
routes.quote: The gully and knife-edge are usually snow-free
snowSentences: [seasonal_guidance] The gully and knife-edge are usually snow-free, but little shade on the burned trail makes midday very hot.
[seasonal_guidance] Snow often lingers in the loose approach gully and on the north side of the ridge, and the upper forest roads may still hold snow.
[seasonal_guidance] Peak larch color early in the month, but snow flurries can coat the 5.7 step and the loose gully, so watch the forecast.
[seasonal_guidance] Snow and ice on the knife-edge and gully, and the forest roads to the trailhead can become snowbound.

[best_season] Popular in late September/early October for golden larches in the basins below, though the route is in shape anytime the approach gully and ridge are snow-free, roughly late June through October.

routes.name: East Peak (Northeast Ridge to East Face)
routes.whyDry: Pass and basin snow-free in the late July-September window.
routes.quote: after the snow clears from Ingalls Pass and the basin
snowSentences: [approach] From the lake, head toward the east side of the peak, keeping to the right of the large couloir there.
[seasonal_guidance] Late July to September, after the snow clears from Ingalls Pass and the basin and the loose upper face is dry .
[seasonal_guidance] Snow melts off Ingalls Pass and the ledges to the ridge base through the month;
[seasonal_guidance] early July may still need care on snow patches.
[seasonal_guidance] Snow and ice linger near Ingalls Pass and throughout the basin, and the ledges to the ridge can be snow-covered;
[seasonal_guidance] the approach is snow-free, though afternoon thunderstorms are common.
[seasonal_guidance] Early snow or ice on the poorly protected upper face turns a 5.6 X pitch dangerous, and days are short.

routes.name: Standard Scramble (Appleton Pass / Boulder Lake approach)
routes.whyDry: Snow near the pass only into July; peak season is talus and meadow.
routes.quote: Snow near the pass and in the basin below the summit into July
snowSentences: [hazards] Lingering snow near Appleton Pass and in the basin below the summit into July;
[hazards] NPS recommends an ice axe and self-arrest skills for early-season travel on the approach trail.
[obj_haz] lingering snowfields into early summer .
[obj_haz] wet, heavy maritime snow common in the Olympics, carrying avalanche risk in winter/spring .
[gear] ice axe (recommended by NPS for the trail approach in early season / on residual snow) .
[what_to_bring] ice axe (early season) .
[seasonal_guidance] Start of the stated best-season window, but lingering snow near Appleton Pass is called out in the existing hazards, so early July can still have patchy snow .
[seasonal_guidance] Full snow conditions;

routes.name: Southwest Slopes
routes.whyDry: Couloir snow is early-mid season and has a heather-ramp alternative; no glacier on route.
routes.quote: or the broken heather/cliff ramps to its left
snowSentences: [beta] No other named technical route (rock face, ridge, or couloir line) is documented on this peak;
[hazards] steep snow/ice in the Silent Lakes approach couloir, the technical crux of the trip (not the summit scrambling);
[hazards] it degrades into a loose rock gully by late season .
[obj_haz] Lingering snowfields on the Easy Pass Trail into early summer;
[obj_haz] NPS advises carrying an ice axe .
[watch_out] The Silent Lakes headwall couloir/gully is the technical crux of the trip, not the class 3 summit scrambling.
[gear] ice axe (useful into July, especially on Easy Pass's north side and the Silent Lakes headwall) .
[gear] crampons (early/mid-season for the Silent Lakes approach couloir) .

routes.name: East Slopes (via Airplane Lake)
routes.whyDry: Upper east-face snow only into July; season late July-September.
routes.quote: lingering snow on the upper east slopes into July .
snowSentences: [overview] Mount Saul is the fourth-highest point on Wenatchee Ridge, a spur of the Cascade crest in the Glacier Peak Wilderness.

[beta] From the lake, either kick up the east slope and east face (a snow climb early in the season) or gain the ridge north of the lake through a saddle and follow it to the summit, finishing with class 3 scrambling on rock that is solid in places and loose in others.
[hazards] Stream crossings of the White River and Indian Creek that get noticeably harder in the afternoon as snowmelt raises water levels .
[hazards] Lingering snow on the upper east face/slopes into July (continuous above ~4,700 ft in one logged July ascent), requiring an ice axe and step-kicking skills .
[obj_haz] lingering snow on the approach and ridge in early season .
[gear] ice axe (early season) .
[what_to_bring] Ice axe (and microspikes/light crampons for early-season snow on the upper mountain) .

[descent_text] whichever way is chosen, time creek crossings on Indian Creek/the White River for morning (lower, easier water) rather than late afternoon, when snowmelt runoff makes fords more difficult.

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.whyDry: Gully snow is a winter/spring condition; summer gully is dry.
routes.quote: gully and ridge typically snow-free;
snowSentences: [beta] In winter and spring a snow gully below the summit ridge is often climbed instead, and many parties rope up for it.
[hazards] Cornices and avalanche terrain in and above the summit gully during winter/spring ascents .
[obj_haz] Snow/ice-filled gully below the summit ridge in winter and spring .
[gear] ice axe (early season) .
[what_to_bring] Ice axe and crampons for winter/spring ascents when the gully is snow or ice-filled .
[pro_needs] In winter and spring some parties rope up or fix a hand line on the snow gully below the summit ridge.
[approach] expect a mix of dirt, talus, and (in early season) snow, with the gully becoming genuinely difficult — muddy, loose, and exposed — once it melts out in mid-to-late summer.

[descent_text] In dry, snow-free conditions most parties downclimb the gully directly (it's an easy-4th-class scramble on dirt and rock), then reverse the cross-country traverse past the pond near point 4875 back to the climbers' path, and follow that path and the closed road back down to the gate.

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.whyDry: Snow lingers only into early-to-mid July.
routes.quote: a dry-rock, snow-free window from late July through September is the sweet spot
snowSentences: [beta] Winter ascents are possible with snow coverage on the southwest ridge when avalanche conditions are stable.
[hazards] Lingering snow/postholing on the approach and lower slope into early summer .
[approach] This upper slope holds snow into early summer and can present avalanche/glissade hazard in spring conditions;
[seasonal_guidance] Late July through September — this window has the driest talus and lowest residual-snow risk in the summit gullies .
[seasonal_guidance] Trail is generally in, but early-season snow can still linger in the upper gully sections early in the month .
[seasonal_guidance] Shorter daylight and the first snow/freeze events of fall can return, adding to the already-loose footing on the summit slopes .
[seasonal_hazards] N/A - no glacier travel .

[best_season] snow typically lingers in Commonwealth Basin and on the upper slope into early-to-mid July, and the fractured rock becomes genuinely unsafe when wet, so a dry-rock, snow-free window from late July through September is the sweet spot.

routes.name: Southeast Ridge
routes.whyDry: Snow is early-season; summer ascents are snow-free.
routes.quote: mid/late-summer ascents (July) are snow-free
snowSentences: [beta] From the tarn, climb the loose scree slope (snow-covered in early season) north of the tarn to a gap in the southeast ridge, then turn left (north-west) and follow the ridge about a mile over several false summits — mostly class 2 walking with a few class 3 sections and a narrow, exposed crux just below the true summit.
[hazards] Creek crossings (Robinson Creek, Beauty Creek, and the West Fork Beauty Creek tributary) can run high during spring snowmelt.
[hazards] Breakable snow crust over downed logs in the forested lower approach has been reported in late-May conditions.
[obj_haz] early-season cornices/steep snow .
[watch_out] The scree slope below the ridge gap is loose and can be snow-covered and slick in early season.
[gear] ice axe (early-season snow in the cirque/chute) .
[what_to_bring] ice axe — snow slope below the ridge crest .
[what_to_bring] crampons — early season, snow slope below the ridge crest .

routes.name: West Route
routes.whyDry: Freezer Pass snow lingers only to early-mid July.
routes.quote: Peak dry-season window - talus and heather slopes are snow-free
snowSentences: [overview] A pair of pyramidal twin summits in the Entiat Mountains subrange of the North Cascades, within the Glacier Peak Wilderness on Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Wenatchee River Ranger District) land in Chelan County.
[hazards] Lingering snow/ice on the Freezer Pass traverse into early-mid July .
[obj_haz] Residual snow/ice in the crux gully into early summer .
[gear] Ice axe (and crampons in early season, roughly through mid-July) for the Freezer Pass traverse if snow lingers .

[approach] Follow Phelps Creek Trail #1511 up the east side of the valley — a gentle, well-graded grade of roughly 275 ft per mile — crossing into the Glacier Peak Wilderness at 2.6 miles and reaching the Leroy Creek ford at about 3.5 miles.
[approach] snow can linger on this stretch into early or mid July.

[descent_text] From there retrace the traverse west: cross the washed-out gully at about 6,600 ft, keeping the party strung out in a line rather than stacked, and sidehill back across the loose scrub and rock to the west shore of Lower Ice Lake.
[seasonal_guidance] Early July can still hold lingering snow on the approach and west-facing slopes and higher creek crossings;

routes.name: Standard Scramble
routes.whyDry: Headlee Pass snow-free July-September.
routes.quote: July through September - talus and slabs are snow-free and the Headlee Pass approach is clearest
snowSentences: [hazards] Lingering snow into midsummer on shaded aspects;
[hazards] ice axe/crampons often still needed into July in the Headlee Pass gully .
[obj_haz] Headlee Pass snow/ice (many reported accidents/injuries) .
[gear] Ice axe and crampons (spring/early-season snow) .
[what_to_bring] Ice axe/crampons if any snow remains on the approach .
[what_to_bring] ice axe — early season, snow in the basin .
[approach] this ford can be genuinely difficult and dangerous after heavy rain or early-season snowmelt.

[approach] From the basin the trail steepens sharply into a narrow, loose rock chute switchbacking up to Headlee Pass (4,720 ft, about 2.7 miles from the trailhead) — this chute is notorious for rockfall dislodged by parties above and is also an avalanche path in shoulder-season/spring snow conditions, so groups should spread out and move through it deliberately.

routes.name: South Coulior
routes.whyDry: Snow couloir is an early-season option only.
routes.quote: Early in the season the south couloir itself is an option
snowSentences: [approach] Early in the season the south couloir itself is an option, entered from the Dartmouth Basin side or from the Lower Saddle by staying left of the rib that divides it from the Exum gully.
[descent_text] If you followed the couloir in early season, snow can be steep and exposed rock loose, so an axe and crampons are prudent on the way down.

routes.name: Northeast Face R of Warrior I
routes.whyDry: Couloir snow is early season and on an avoided walk-off.
routes.quote: with a couloir that can hold steep snow early in the season.
snowSentences: [descent_text] A walk-off toward the Warbonnet side is loose, slow and best avoided, with a couloir that can hold steep snow early in the season.
